title: Your repo after init
subtitle: Every place lighthouse init writes: whose it is, where it comes from, and what --upgrade does with it.

areas.label: AGENTS.md
areas.about: The instructions every coding agent in the repo reads: your own text plus one block per package.
areas.how: Init adds one managed block per package and leaves the rest of the file as it is.
areas.upgrade: Replaces or removes only lighthouse's blocks; your text stays. If you changed or deleted a part of lighthouse's, --upgrade stops and writes nothing until you pass --force, which overwrites your change.

areas.label: CLAUDE.md
areas.about: The file Claude Code reads; it imports AGENTS.md so both read the same rules.
areas.how: Init writes the single line @AGENTS.md, only when neither AGENTS.md nor CLAUDE.md exists. An existing CLAUDE.md is never changed; init warns when it lacks the import.
areas.upgrade: Same rule: written only when both files are missing. An existing CLAUDE.md is never touched.

areas.label: lighthouse.toml
areas.about: Your project's settings for lighthouse: language, forge, test gate and more.
areas.how: Init adds the tables and keys that are missing and never changes a value that is already there.
areas.upgrade: Adds only missing keys. Keys of a package you removed stay, and a deleted key of lighthouse's comes back in the diff you approve, without a refusal.

areas.label: .claude/hooks/lighthouse/
areas.about: Scripts that Claude Code runs around tool calls, prompts and stops, such as the commit gate.
areas.how: Whole files, copied from the hooks of each package.
areas.upgrade: Replaces them and removes files a package no longer ships. If you changed or deleted a part of lighthouse's, --upgrade stops and writes nothing until you pass --force, which overwrites your change.

areas.label: .claude/skills/lighthouse-*/
areas.about: The lighthouse skills Claude Code can run, one folder per skill.
areas.how: Whole files, copied from the skills of each package.
areas.upgrade: Replaces them and removes files a package no longer ships. If you changed or deleted a part of lighthouse's, --upgrade stops and writes nothing until you pass --force, which overwrites your change.

areas.label: .agents/skills/lighthouse-*/
areas.about: The same skills for Codex and OpenCode.
areas.how: Whole files, copied from the skills of each package.
areas.upgrade: Replaces them and removes files a package no longer ships. If you changed or deleted a part of lighthouse's, --upgrade stops and writes nothing until you pass --force, which overwrites your change.

areas.label: .claude/agents/lighthouse-*.md
areas.about: The lighthouse subagents Claude Code can start.
areas.how: Whole files, copied from the agents of the core package.
areas.upgrade: Replaces them and removes files the package no longer ships. If you changed or deleted a part of lighthouse's, --upgrade stops and writes nothing until you pass --force, which overwrites your change.

areas.label: .claude/settings.json
areas.about: Claude Code's settings: lighthouse registers its hooks and permissions here next to yours.
areas.how: Init merges lighthouse's hook registrations and permissions.allow rules into the file; everything else is yours.
areas.upgrade: Replaces only lighthouse's hooks and rules; the rest of the file stays. If you changed or deleted a part of lighthouse's, --upgrade stops and writes nothing until you pass --force, which overwrites your change.

areas.label: .lighthouse/lib/lighthouse_lib/
areas.about: The shared Python code that lighthouse's skills and hooks import.
areas.how: Whole files, copied from the lib of each package.
areas.upgrade: Replaces them and removes files a package no longer ships. If you changed or deleted a part of lighthouse's, --upgrade stops and writes nothing until you pass --force, which overwrites your change.

areas.label: .lighthouse/scripts/
areas.about: The helper scripts that lighthouse's skills run.
areas.how: Whole files, copied from the scripts of each package.
areas.upgrade: Replaces them and removes files a package no longer ships. If you changed or deleted a part of lighthouse's, --upgrade stops and writes nothing until you pass --force, which overwrites your change.

areas.label: .lighthouse/headings.toml
areas.about: The table of headings that issues and pull requests must use, per language.
areas.how: One whole file, copied from the core package.
areas.upgrade: Replaces it. If you changed or deleted a part of lighthouse's, --upgrade stops and writes nothing until you pass --force, which overwrites your change.

areas.label: .lighthouse/manifest.toml
areas.about: The record of what lighthouse installed, so --upgrade knows what it may replace.
areas.how: Written by init: the record of what lighthouse installed.
areas.upgrade: Rewritten whenever the installed units or the lighthouse version change; an unchanged run leaves it as it is.

areas.label: .github/pull_request_template.md
areas.about: The pull request template GitHub offers on every new pull request.
areas.how: One whole file, copied from the core package.
areas.upgrade: Replaces it. If you changed or deleted a part of lighthouse's, --upgrade stops and writes nothing until you pass --force, which overwrites your change.

areas.label: .github/workflows/lighthouse-*.yml
areas.about: The GitHub Actions workflows of lighthouse.
areas.how: Whole files, with the @@key@@ placeholders filled from lighthouse.toml. A workflow is installed only when every key it needs is set; otherwise init reports it and skips it.
areas.upgrade: Replaces a workflow when every key is set; when one is missing, the installed workflow stays as it is. If you changed or deleted a part of lighthouse's, --upgrade stops and writes nothing until you pass --force, which overwrites your change.

areas.label: ~/.config/lighthouse/host.toml
areas.about: Settings of this workstation, such as its Tailscale address, for lighthouse usage and serve.
areas.how: Written by init only, only when Tailscale identifies the host; it asks first, unless you pass --yes.
areas.upgrade: Only reports a note when the file is missing.
